scope: Fifteen bounded, individually sourced chronology strands. No automatic cross-strand alignment, no absolute AR date conversion and no assertions that a narrated legend is historical fact. The Gatewatch founding strand uses the official Battle for Zendikar retrospective and contemporaneous Oath/Last Stand episodes, not real-world set release order; it establishes only the founding episode on Zendikar, not the complete Gatewatch biography. The Thran-to-invasion strand uses the 2008 Wizards historical retrospective and does not decide the order between Old Phyrexia's decimation and Yawgmoth's destruction. The Dominaria-to-Kamigawa fracture sequence quotes explicit cross-plane cause, but does not globally align all plane eras. The Alara strand places Gideon's isolated-Bant arrival before the Conflux without assigning a cause to Alara's unknown original Sundering; wars concurrent with border dissolution are not forced into a BEFORE relation. The New Phyrexia strand describes early Mirrodin conquest, not post-March of the Machine politics. The early Meditation Realm strand is Ugin's remembered conflict; the distinct War of the Spark-to-Dragonstorm strand tracks later imprisonment and escape without claiming either dragon's death, present location or current spark state. The Amonkhet-to-Ravnica strand preserves Samut's firsthand warning and the Eternal flow's later shutdown as bounded, separate sequences; it does not invent a total interplane event order.

strands.title: Bolas's 2019 imprisonment, the Tarkir: Dragonstorm escape, and Ajani's later report
strands.limitation: The 2019 editorial ending and later official fiction establish imprisonment and escape, not that the old prison still holds. Narset sees both dragons vanish into an unknown void and explicitly questions whether they died; Ajani later reports the escape but says Bolas's spark state is unknown. Neither a confirmed death, restored spark, destination, nor an absolute in-universe date follows. This W strand is NOT merged with Ugin's ancient B-strand recollections.

nodes.label: Bolas loses his spark and is imprisoned under Ugin after War of the Spark
The Meditation Realm unravels during Tarkir: Dragonstorm
Bolas's restraints come undone as the Meditation Realm burns
Ugin tries and fails to restrain Bolas as he rises
Bolas and Ugin vanish from Narset's view, with their fate uncertain
Narset crosses an Omenpath out of the collapsing Realm
Ajani later tells Liliana of Bolas's escape and uncertain spark

edges.quote: there was Bolas, laughing ecstatically, as his fetters came undone
edges.note: The same Bolas previously imprisoned under Ugin in the 2019 official account is released from restraints; this does not prove regained planeswalking ability.

edges.quote: The Omenpath gleamed like a star as the rest of the Meditation Realm burned away to that terrible nothing.
edges.note: The described unraveling is already in progress before Narset subsequently passes through the Omenpath; not an asserted order against the exact instant Bolas's fetters break.

edges.quote: as his fetters came undone; Bolas rising into that emptiness as Ugin flung himself at his brother
edges.note: Ugin attempts to seize Bolas as the just-freed dragon rises; the scene gives no outcome beyond the failed immediate attempt.

edges.quote: trying to hold him in place, trying and failing; Bolas and Ugin winking out of existence
edges.note: Narset observes their disappearance after Ugin's failed restraint; her following 'dead now, perhaps' explicitly does NOT establish confirmed death.

edges.quote: Crossing the threshold felt like she was stepping through a pool of silver
edges.note: The story describes Narset crossing the escape threshold after witnessing both brothers vanish; it does not establish the brothers' destinations.

edges.quote: I was on Tarkir. I helped Elspeth and Narset stop them. We wound up following the signs back to the Meditation Realm
edges.note: Ajani recounts the Realm expedition in the past tense in a later conversation with Liliana; his uncertainty about Bolas's spark remains in force.

strands.title: Alara — unknown Sundering, Gideon's isolated Bant arrival, Conflux and simultaneous shard wars
strands.limitation: The 2015 Worlds of Magic Origins feature explicitly locates Gideon's arrival during Bant's isolation and before the subsequent reunion; it calls Alara's original sundering cataclysm UNKNOWN. The Alara plane overview describes post-reunion five-color mana and wars as former shard boundaries dissolve. Conflux, boundary dissolution and the outbreak of fighting overlap in the prose: a DURING_OR_AFTER_START relation is NOT a strict before/after date. No Dominarian AR date, cause of the original cataclysm, or causal identity with Nicol Bolas's later conspiracy is inferred.

nodes.label: An unidentified cataclysm sunders Alara into five shards
Alara's five shards evolve separately over centuries
Gideon arrives on Bant while it remains isolated
Alara's five shards converge into a single plane
The reunited Alara again has all five mana colors
Boundaries between reunited Alaran shards dissolve
Formerly isolated shard cultures clash as their borders dissolve

edges.quote: Sundered by some unknown cataclysm, their environments and cultures evolved independently
edges.note: An unidentified Sundering precedes the separate evolution of the shard civilizations; the cataclysm's cause is not identified.

edges.quote: at the time of Gideon's arrival, Bant was entirely isolated
edges.note: The period of separation already existed when Gideon arrived; this is NOT a claim that isolation had ended by his arrival.

edges.quote: Alara has since been reunited, and Bant is now one region on a larger plane. But at the time of Gideon's arrival, Bant was entirely isolated
edges.note: The retrospective explicitly distinguishes Gideon's isolated-Bant visit from the later reunion.

edges.quote: they have converged into one, and the rejoined plane flows with all five colors of mana once more
edges.note: Five-color mana describes Alara after the shards have rejoined, without any AR calendar conversion.

edges.quote: As the boundaries between the shards dissolve, cultures clash and wars ensue.
edges.note: The plane overview describes reunification and dissolving former borders as the same transition, not strictly ordered completed events.

edges.quote: As the boundaries between the shards dissolve, cultures clash and wars ensue.
edges.note: The wars begin AS borders dissolve, not after every border has finished dissolving; deliberately not a BEFORE edge.

strands.title: Zendikar — Eldrazi prison, Gideon's return, Sea Gate, Gatewatch oaths and the titans' defeat
strands.limitation: This is the bounded Battle for Zendikar / Oath of the Gatewatch founding story, not the complete Gatewatch history. The initial Eye activation releases broods while the titans remain confined; Nissa breaks their remaining bonds later. The later temporary Ulamog-only hedron trap is a distinct event, then Ob Nixilis disrupts it. The founding four are Gideon, Jace, Nissa and Chandra, not the membership of the Gatewatch in any later era. The apparent deaths of Ulamog and Kozilek are explicitly attested in the next official story; Ugin raises the uncertainty of the Multiverse-wide consequences, not a claim that the titans survived. None of these events is dated to an absolute AR year or merged with another strand.

Bolas arranges Jace, Chandra and Sarkhan's reactivation of the Eye

Gideon arrives on Zendikar while searching for Chandra

edges.quote: A little more than a thousand years ago, the Eldrazi nearly escaped—and neither Sorin nor Ugin returned to help.
edges.note: The ancient imprisonment predated the near escape and Nahiri's independent repair; the time phrase is relative, not an AR date.

edges.quote: Then, for reasons of his own, the elder dragon Planeswalker Nicol Bolas arranged for three Planeswalkers to converge on the Eye and unknowingly reactivate it.
edges.note: The retrospective introduces this later Bolas arrangement after Nahiri's repair and departure; it does not identify Bolas as the original prison's creator or destroyer.

edges.quote: The activation of the Eye loosed teeming broods of Eldrazi upon the plane, but the titans themselves were not yet free.
edges.note: The Eye activation does NOT release the titans: that happens when Nissa breaks the remaining bonds in the next passage.

edges.quote: It was then that Gideon Jura first arrived on Zendikar, after following Chandra's trail to the plane
edges.note: The narrated arrival follows Nissa's liberation of the titans and their initial feeding; it is not dated by set release order.

edges.quote: Vowing to return, he left in search of aid at the center of Planeswalker activity: the city-world of Ravnica.
edges.note: Gideon's decision to seek Ravnica allies follows his arrival and initial failed resistance on Zendikar.

edges.quote: Together, Gideon and Jace returned to Zendikar to face the threat of the Eldrazi.
edges.note: The subsequent Sea Gate campaign follows Gideon returning with the recruited Jace; recruitment is not the same as the founding oath.

edges.quote: As they savored their first moments of victory, the merfolk Jori En returned with dire news—the Eldrazi titan Ulamog himself was headed towards Sea Gate.
edges.note: The defenders first retake Sea Gate, then face and temporarily trap Ulamog; the later destruction of Sea Gate is distinct.

edges.quote: knocked the hedrons out of alignment to siphon their energy and reignite his Planeswalker spark.
edges.note: Ob Nixilis sabotages an already aligned prison, releasing its captive titan.

edges.quote: but Ob Nixilis had called Kozilek, one of the other Eldrazi titans, from beneath Zendikar's surface.
edges.note: The account associates Kozilek's renewed appearance with Ob Nixilis's intervention; no absolute elapsed time is inferred.

edges.quote: When the Eldrazi destroyed Sea Gate, they threatened all I believe.
edges.note: Gideon's oath explicitly refers back to the destructive two-titan crisis; the sworn team is the original four only.

edges.quote: Chandra knew this was what she and her friends had come to put to an end. This was their mission. It was their oath.
edges.note: Chandra recalls their oath during the subsequent climactic spell. The official aftermath independently confirms both titans died; it does not settle Ugin's longer-range cautions.

edges.quote: The Eldrazi titans have been destroyed. The world of Zendikar has been saved. Now the four Planeswalkers who acted to make this so must decide what is to come next.
edges.note: The subsequent official account explicitly identifies the titans' destruction as past and the surviving team's next plans as present.

strands.title: Amonkhet to Ravnica — Samut's warning, Eternal transport and Planar Bridge shutdown
strands.limitation: Samut's firsthand statement on Ravnica places the devastation of her Amonkhet home before her warning. Jace's concurrent account identifies the ongoing Planar Bridge flow from Amonkhet and its planned shutdown, while Rat later reports that flow stopped. These are partial source-local comparisons, not one continuous global sequence: the exact timing of the Amonkhet Hours against the Bridge's first activation and the order of every War of the Spark mission are not independently established. Neither story publication dates nor mechanical card-set release order creates an event-order edge.

nodes.label: Bolas devastates Amonkhet; a few survivors remain
Samut warns the Ravnica war council about Amonkhet's fate
Eternals begin entering Ravnica from Amonkhet through the Planar Bridge
The Ravnica council plans to shut down the Planar Bridge from its Amonkhet side
The Planar Bridge and flow of Eternals from Amonkhet have been shut down

edges.quote: Bolas left my world completely desolated. Even now, a mere handful of survivors struggle to defeat the monsters that Nicol Bolas left behind to slaughter us.
edges.note: Samut speaks on Ravnica about her already devastated home, Amonkhet. Her firsthand report is dated only relative to this war council, not to an AR year.

edges.quote: The Planar Bridge from Amonkhet allows a seemingly endless army of Eternals to enter Ravnica and slay the Planeswalkers lured by the Beacon and held by the Sun. We have to shut it down
edges.note: Jace describes Eternals already entering Ravnica before stating the plan to stop the existing flow; arrival continues during the discussion.

edges.quote: The Izzet's Beacon, the Immortal Sun, the Planar Bridge, and the flow of Eternals from Amonkhet had all been shut down.
edges.note: The past-perfect shutdown presupposes the earlier flow. It does not date the exact moment the portal first opened or establish a strict order with Samut's warning.

strands.title: Serra's Realm — Urza's refuge, the Phyrexian incursion and collapse
strands.limitation: The 2008 official summary recounts one historical sequence; it does not prove a complete angel/faction chronology, the timing of Radiant's administration against the final powerstone collapse, or any exact AR date.

edges.quote: This artificial plane was created by the planeswalker Serra to exemplify her love of peace and law.
edges.note: Creation necessarily precedes Urza entering the already existing realm; source gives no calendar year.

edges.quote: When Urza fled here to escape Phyrexian pursuers, Serra and her angels nursed him back to health.
edges.note: The nursing follows Urza's arrival.

edges.quote: Serra and her angels nursed him back to health. But the Phyrexians found the realm and attacked
edges.note: The summary places Phyrexian intrusion after Urza's convalescence; no precision beyond this sequence.

edges.quote: But the Phyrexians found the realm and attacked, tainting it with black mana. Serra abandoned the plane, heartbroken by its corruption.
edges.note: Serra's departure follows corruption caused by the attack.

edges.quote: One of her archangels, Radiant, assumed control of the plane in Serra's absence.
edges.note: Assumption of rule follows Serra's absence.

edges.quote: One of her archangels, Radiant, assumed control of the plane in Serra's absence. But in her zeal to rid the plane of Phyrexian taint, Radiant became draconian and paranoid.
edges.note: The 2008 account describes Radiant's increasingly harsh rule after she assumes control, but does not position this development against Urza's final extraction.

edges.quote: Without its creator, Serra's Realm was slowly collapsing. Urza, seeking a mana source intense enough to power the skyship Weatherlight, hastened its demise by forcibly collapsing the plane's energies into a powerstone
edges.note: The fatal powerstone extraction follows Serra's absence; the guide does not order it against the exact span of Radiant's rule.
